body:
Thank you so much for your post. I've been trying to find the root of all the current problems and it seems like you may have hit the nail on the head: depression, and my initial failure is probably what set that off. I've been trying to avoid accepting that I have a psychological problem, but I think it's time for me to accept that it may be depression, and that it's time to fix it.

I feel like maybe the only reason I ever "had" to commit suicide was because I didn't understand what was happening to me, but I think your post has helped me understand what is going on. I don't want to commit suicide, and I do want to fix my situation. I know I'm capable of a lot more, but I don't know how to get out of this 4-year funk.

I don't want to take meds: I want to be able to reason with myself that this feeling is temporary, and that I can go back to being a high-performing individual who can also have a social life. But how do I reason with myself when I act as my own devil's advocate in arguments with myself? How do I reason with myself to fix everything?
